text: A crew transfer vessel experienced a carbon monoxide leak. A crew transfer vessel was mid-water, waiting for the weather conditions to improve before completing their transfer, when the carbon monoxide alarm in the crew saloon area activated. The detector showed the maximum reading of 200ppm. The crew opened the doors to allow fresh air into the space and the level dropped to 20ppm. The crew decided to return to shore at slow speed with all the doors and windows open to keep the vessel ventilated. The passengers and crew were disembarked and went to hospital as a precautionary measure, but no one had sustained any carbon monoxide poisoning. The cause of the leak was because the exhaust fumes from the vessel's boiler system were venting into the saloon area and the galley extractor fan was turned off. The company organised for an engineer to attend the vessel to assess the boiler exhaust for any issues.
